newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel market quiet, values steady.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel market quiet, values steady.

text.p: Straight-run fuel oil buyers hung back on Monday, becalming the market, while sellers hoped the recent price slide had stopped, traders said.
Offers were just slightly below levels set by a Friday deal by a U.K. refiner to a U.S. buyer, which was heard done at $95.50 fob. Material was heard available prompt.
An Antwerp refiner sold 2,500 tonnes into the barge market at $96 fob, $1 less than on Friday.
There was little buying interest in what was a quiet day for all fuel oil markets. Scandinavian material may have been sold today or on Friday to the U.S. but this could not be confirmed.
"Its all a bit fragile at the moment with no-one really knowing where things are going," said one trader.
A Russian high sulphur straight-run cargo was heard unsold in the Mediterranean, reflecting continuing refiner preference for running more profitable crude through their plant.
